subject: PulsePay integration: toolchain decisions & SDK/auth routing follow-ups
messages:

Subject: PulsePay discovery follow-up — integration priorities

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — very helpful. Quick recap of what matters to the PulsePay engineering team so we can prioritize the POC:

- SDK & onboarding: we want a Node + Python quickstart that shows auth flows and how to call function/tool hooks.
- Auth/residency: enterprise needs OIDC + token introspection; some customers will demand mTLS for on-prem connectors. Data residency (EU customers) is critical.
- Routing & failover: routing by region (eu/us) and a fallback to a smaller open model when dedicated capacity is saturated.
- Structured output & tool calling: we need a JSON schema for transaction parsing and a clear manifest for tools the model can call (e.g., KYC lookup, payments API).
- Embeddings & rerank: search over transaction docs + a reranker. Prefer embeddings to never leave our VPC for sensitive data.

Open questions for you:
1) Can Redwood support a hybrid auth mode (OIDC primary, optional mTLS for on-prem)?
2) Is it possible to run embeddings in-customer VPC and push only vectors to Redwood for reranking?
3) Recommended patterns for parallel tool calls with aggregation and consistent error handling?

We'd like a short mutual action plan and an initial architecture sketch before the PO. Can you share a one-page design and recommended SDK steps by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Alice Murray
Head of ML Engineering, PulsePay

Attachments: pulsepay-requirements-2028-05-08.pdf (pdf)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PulsePay discovery follow-up — integration priorities

Alice — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise response + proposed next steps. I also attached a short integration outline and an SDK quickstart draft (stubs) for the POC.

Short answers to your questions:
- Hybrid auth: yes. Recommend OIDC for cloud-hosted flows (fine-grained scopes + introspection). Provide mTLS only for on-prem connectors where customers require mutual auth. We can support both; the SDK will surface an AuthProvider interface and sample configs for both modes.

- Embeddings residency: two options depending on your compliance posture:
  1) Customer-hosted embeddings: run the embedder in your VPC, store vectors in your vector DB, and call Redwood only for the reranker/generation step. We can accept pointer-based inputs (IDs + retrieval context) rather than raw vectors.
  2) Redwood-hosted vectors with VPC peering: vectors live in a customer-controlled subnet and Redwood has access via peered connection and ACLs.

- Parallel tool calls & aggregation pattern (recommended):
  1) Tool manifest: define each tool in a small JSON/YAML manifest with fields: name, id, input_schema (JSON Schema), timeout_ms, retry_policy, idempotency_key_required.
  2) Orchestrator model call: model returns a structured orchestration object (tools: [ {name, args, run_in_parallel: true/false} ]).
  3) Execution engine: spawn parallel calls for run_in_parallel=true with a bounded worker pool and per-tool circuit breakers. Aggregate results into a single 'tool_responses' array sorted by tool priority.
  4) Error handling: on tool failure apply per-tool fallback (cached value, mock response) or escalate back to model with a standardized error token so model can decide alternative steps.

Design trade-offs we recommend:
- Parallelism increases throughput but needs strict idempotency and end-to-end tracing (request_id) to avoid duplicate side effects.
- For payments/KYC, prefer synchronous single-call tools with short timeouts + retry=0 for side-effecting ops; use async callbacks/webhooks for long-running backends.

Structured output suggestion (top-level JSON schema excerpt):
{
  "request_id": "string",
  "intent": "string",
  "entities": [ {"type":"string","value":"string"} ],
  "tools": [ {"name":"string","args":{},"mode":"sync|async","priority":int} ],
  "embeds_query": {"vector_id":"string|null","top_k":int},
  "response_v1": {"answer":"string","confidence":float}
}

POC proposal and timeline:
- Day 0–2: Finalize M.A.P. (mutual action plan) and confirm POC scope (we propose: SDK quickstart, one payments tool + one KYC tool, embeddings retrieval + local reranker).
- Week 1: Provide SDK quickstart, sample tool manifests, and integration-outline.yaml (attached).
- Week 2: Run POC with test dataset (we'll provide sample prompts and evaluation checklist).

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Vivek: deliver integration-outline.yaml + SDK quickstart by EOD tomorrow (ATTACHED).
- Marissa: prepare the POC evaluation prompts and success criteria (cc'd).
- Priyom: scope infra requirements for VPC peering and vector residency.
- Alice/Ben: confirm POC resources and whether any customers are in-scope for the initial run.

If that looks good I'll book a 30-min sync for Thu morning to walk through the outline.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: pulsepay-integration-outline.yaml (yaml), redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (md)

Vivek — this is helpful, thanks. Couple clarifications:

- Residency: PulsePay will start with US customers but we absolutely need EU-only flows for our EU merchant base. For the POC please assume embeddings must remain inside PulsePay's EU VPC for EU datasets. That means option (1) you listed is preferred for EU, option (2) acceptable for US.
- Reranker: we prefer the reranker to be a small footprint model running in our infra (so we can A/B) and use Redwood only for the generation step. Can Redwood’s API accept reranker scores as an input signal for the final rank+answer?
- Tool semantics: KYC lookup is read-only and can be parallelized; payments/settlement call must be single-threaded and strictly idempotent. We need examples for per-tool retry_policy and how the SDK surfaces idempotency keys.

We can allocate 2 engineers for the POC (Ben + me). Thu morning sync works — can you send a calendar invite?

Thanks,
Alice
